mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected corporate cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the tightening phase (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for ≥ 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 7% signals labor market tightening, raising wage growth expectations and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite UNRATE > 7% for ≥ 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST (household spending index) exceeds 1.5% above its 12-month moving average, it indicates accelerating consumer demand, which is associated with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or insignificant during the defined acceleration period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 suggests supply-side softness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative over 3 consecutive contraction months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 (GDP personal consumption) imply dual disinflationary pressure, reducing growth expectations and driving negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the co-move of declining rates and weak consumption.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS (employment months) rises by more than 50,000 month-over-month for two consecutive months, it suggests labor market resilience, supporting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase > 50,000 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the defined employment momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% and increase in RSAFS (retail sales) above 2% indicates demand is outpacing inflation, which is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant during the defined inflation-outpacing sales pattern.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE and HOUST both show upward momentum (UNRATE rising > 0.2% and HOUST rising > 0.5% over the prior 3 months), it signals improving labor and consumption conditions, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns regardless of macro regime.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite the defined upward momentum in both labor and consumption indicators.
